title: Finite free change of rings exchanges quotient completion on arbitrary complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and $R\to S$ a map of sheaves of commutative rings. Suppose $S\cong R^{\oplus d}$ as an $R$-module sheaf for some finite $d\geq0$. Let $t\in R(1)$ and $v\in S(1)$ be global sections with injective multiplication on their respective rings, and suppose the image of $t$ is $uv^e$ for a unit $u\in S(1)^\times$ and an integer $e\geq1$. Assume countable products of $R$-modules, $S$-modules and abelian sheaves are exact. Use the unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived change of rings $T=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and the strict quotient completions
$$C_RQ=R\lim_{n\geq1}(Q\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/t^nR),\qquad C_SH=R\lim_{m\geq1}(H\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}S/v^mS).$$
Here quotients are sheaf quotients, tensors are K-flat total tensors [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and the derived limits and units $\eta^R,\eta^S$ are the strict-tower derived limits [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] with the quotient augmentations, represented by a product map and zero shifted-product component. For every $Q\in D(R)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$\epsilon_Q:T C_RQ\xrightarrow{\sim}C_STQ,\qquad \epsilon_Q\,T(\eta^R_Q)=\eta^S_{TQ}.$$
It is specified by the canonical tensor/product map on the $t$-tower, the identifications $(R/t^nR)\otimes_R S=S/v^{en}S$, and the inverse of the specified arithmetic-subsequence Roos comparison of [lem-pur-compact-support-roos-cofinality]. It is independent of the basis of $S$. No completeness or boundedness hypothesis on $Q$ is imposed.
